# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 31 (Bu-Vb Pc31)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 31, titled *Āvasathapiṇḍa* ("Eating excessively at a public guesthouse"), establishes an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*) for a monk who partakes of more than one meal at a public alms center or resthouse [SuttaCentral]. According to the origin story and word commentary examined by Ute Hüsken, arriving wandering ascetics originally sought permission from the donor or founder of such a facility to spend the night; the commentary notes that an *āvasatha* does not necessarily imply a formal building, as food could also be provided generally in the open air (*ajjhokāse*), where alms meals were distributed to travelers [Hüsken 1997]. An English translation of the rule and its commentary has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral demonstrate that this precept is widely shared across Vinaya traditions, with counterparts in the Pali Bhikkhu Pātimokkha (Pc 31), the Bhikkhu Parivāra, and the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (Pc 117) [SuttaCentral]. It is further paralleled across Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan Vinayas of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya lineages [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus identifies Pali-internal text reuse with 108 texts, exhibiting substantial shared phrasing with adjacent food-related rules in the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (such as Pc 32, Pc 33, Pc 35, Pc 39, Pd 3, and Pd 4) as well as Khandhaka passages in Kd 1 and Kd 15 [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns segments of this text with Tibetan Vinaya literature, including the *Vinayasaṃgraha* (D4105) [DharmaNexus].
